title: JUDGEBENCH: A BENCHMARK FOR EVALUATING LLM-BASED JUDGES

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the LLM-based judge twice on the same pair of responses by swapping their order in the second trial, and aggregating the results to identify and filter out inconsistent decisions or ties caused by the presentation order.

Conducting an ablation study by using a different underlying model (Claude-3.5-Sonnet instead of GPT-4o) to generate the response pairs, testing whether models are disproportionately challenged when evaluating responses generated by themselves.

Calculating and comparing the average token counts of the correct and incorrect responses across the dataset instances to ensure the benchmark effectively mitigates the judges' tendency to prefer longer responses.

Mitigating the bias by designing the benchmark's pipeline to sample both candidate responses (correct and incorrect) from a single model, thereby reducing the influence of stylistic differences that cause judges to favor their own outputs.
